channel.title: RetroMac
channel.description: Most recent changes with links to updates.

item.title: Version 2.8.1
item.description:
RetroMac 2.8.1

A fix for Exposé, which shipped in 2.8 yesterday.

  • Exposé no longer hides RetroMac’s own windows. The window list skipped anything owned by RetroMac itself — which on a theme desktop is a large share of what you see, since Television, the CPU monitor, Notepad, Calculator and App Folder windows are all ours. With only those open, Exposé reported “No windows” over a screen full of them. Nothing unwanted appears as a result: the dock, Dashboard, the Exposé sheet itself, the desktop pet, menus and desktop icons all sit above the window layer Exposé reads and were already excluded.
  • With a second display attached, the screen that happened to hold no windows announced “No windows” while the other one was showing them all. That message now means what it says — nothing anywhere.

Everything new in 2.8 — Snow Leopard’s own chrome, Dashboard, Exposé, the 10.6 stacks, the Disk Defragmenter, Flurry and phosphor persistence — is included.

item.title: Version 2.8
item.description:
RetroMac 2.8 — Snow Leopard, with Dashboard and Exposé

  • Snow Leopard has its own chrome: 10.6 no longer borrows Cheetah’s early-Aqua look — three themes used to share one window style, so a 2009 desktop wore a 2001 window. The title bar is measured off the original: unified grey, flat traffic lights, the separator along the bottom. With it come blue gel scrollers, period-correct icons for Chrome, iWork, Claude and ChatGPT, and the striped Macintosh HD.
  • Dashboard is back: the widget layer macOS dropped in Catalina, rebuilt. ⌃F12 brings up Clock, Calculator, Weather, Calendar, Stickies, a Google search pill and a CPU monitor. Add and remove them from the bar, drag them where you like, and they stay put.
  • Exposé: every window on the desktop, shrunk so none overlap, each card travelling from where its window actually sits. ⌃F9 for all of them, ⌃F10 for the front app — or hold a dock icon, the way 10.6 changed that gesture to work.
  • Stacks, drawn the way 10.6 drew them: Applications and Downloads open as a grid with real Quick Look previews, sitting next to the Trash where they belong, and hanging from the callout nose that points back at the dock icon.
  • Disk Defragmenter: the Windows 95 and 98 themes get the defrag widget, with its authentic icon, a working scrollbar and a period-correct pace.
  • Desktop extras: the real Flurry screensaver for the Mac OS X themes, five more Snow Leopard wallpapers (Rocks, Earth, Aurora Blue, Zebra, Stones), and an optional tint for the menu bar so a modern translucent one stops fighting the theme.
  • Phosphor persistence: afterglow across frames, applied to the signal ahead of the mask, in every Metal renderer.
  • Settings have a Shader tab: what was “Advanced” is now Shader, and it leads the sidebar. The effect’s settings were spread over three tabs and five sections; they are in one place now — Preset, Look, Where, Per-App, Performance and When.
  • Fixes: the shader’s per-theme on/off is no longer overruled at launch, and switching it off no longer discards the theme’s preset; the Quality picker stops resetting a frame rate you chose, and 120 fps is offered only on panels that reach it; a failed theme import can no longer lose the theme it was replacing; Hover! is genuinely offline; the shader and the dock pin their display by UUID, so they stay put across a reconnect; widgets stop rendering a cached copy of themselves; every readme window can be dragged; and every boot screen shows for the same five seconds.

item.title: Version 2.7
item.description:
RetroMac 2.7 — Windows 95 and the Fun Stuff CD-ROM

  • Windows 95 theme: the one that started it all — solid navy title bars, the silver 3D chrome, the clouds wallpaper, an authentic boot screen and Win95 shell icons. The Start menu is period-correct: large icons in a narrow first level, small ones in the wider submenus, and neither Windows Update nor Log Off, because Windows 95 had neither.
  • Fun Stuff (D:): the CD-ROM is back on the desktop. Browse FUNSTUFF into HOVER, VIDEOS and PICTURES — music videos play in a bare title-bar window, and Clouds.exe / WINBMP.EXE set your wallpaper the way a 1995 CD-ROM would.
  • Hover! plays again: the Microsoft HTML5 remake, self-hosted and fully offline in its classic pixel-graphics mode. No Wine, no emulator, no internet needed.
  • Authentic Win95/98 details: scrollbars with a single arrow at each end, raised bevels and a dithered track; the status bar below its own scrollbar row; the program icon back in the title bar; and no running-app dots on 98/Me/XP, whose taskbars already show what is running.
  • Readmes overhauled: every theme’s About This Theme is closable again, fills its window edge-to-edge, sizes itself so it needs no scrolling, and shows its artwork. Futurama finally has one too.
  • Start into your theme: a new opt-in setting activates your last theme right at launch instead of the clean desktop.
  • Fixes: Windows 95 title bars no longer showed the Windows 98 gradient (which also repaired every Windows 98 Plus! colour scheme); file lists are white instead of grey; desktop icon labels stop colliding; boot videos are no longer cropped; sheep.exe works on Windows 95; Classic Teal is the canonical #008080.

item.title: Version 2.6
item.description:
RetroMac 2.6 — Windows Me joins the family

  • Windows Me theme: Millennium Edition — the brush-script Start-menu banner, a 4K-remastered wallpaper, an authentic boot splash, Me shell icons (oval Recycle Bin, Media Player), and “Windows Update” atop the Start menu, with the full special-theme treatment (system tray, taskbar auto-hide, desktop pet).
  • Windows 7 Aero, rebuilt: a proper glass Start menu with the account picture peeking over the top edge, a real translucent Aero taskbar, and an authentic notification area — a show-hidden-icons chevron, network and volume icons that open the matching macOS settings, and a two-line time/date clock.
  • 100% themes: the marker on the fully-realised themes is now a 100% badge shown after the theme name (Futurama counts too).
  • Flyout upgrades: drag Quick Access tiles to reorder them in Edit mode, double-click the floating button to toggle your last theme, and the menu-bar Apple-logo cycle now includes the Futurama teal apple.
  • New shaders: NLO VHS SP — a real single-pass NTSC comb-demodulation with authentic dot crawl and cross-colour — and CRT EasyMode, a clean, sharp mask-and-scanline CRT.
  • Fixes: Windows 98/Me map Safari to the IE icon and show real Chrome/Firefox icons again; the Activate licence field is no longer white-on-white.

item.title: Version 2.5
item.description:
RetroMac 2.5 — Futurama joins the lineup

  • Futurama theme: a Planet Express take on the desktop. The dock is the show’s riveted metal girder — a pressure-gauge control panel on the left, a recessed glass shelf your icons rest on, and a grille end cap on the right — with a teal Bender-and-friends icon set, the Planet Express wallpaper, a teal Apple logo, and bold cel-shaded window outlines.
  • Restore system cursor: a new button in Cursor settings puts the normal macOS pointer straight back if a themed cursor ever gets stuck, and RetroMac now recovers the cursor reliably on the next launch even if it was force-quit while a themed cursor was active.
  • Fix (all custom docks): minimizing or restoring a window, or changing your pinned apps, now resizes the dock immediately instead of leaving it the wrong size until you moused over it.

item.title: Version 2.4
item.description:
RetroMac 2.4 — NeXTSTEP joins the lineup

  • NeXTSTEP theme: the full NeXT desktop, rebuilt natively — a vertical Workspace menu, a right-edge dock with a live clock/calendar and the Recycler, black title bars with the four-grey chiseled bevel, the MegaPixel wallpaper, and the NeXT cursor. Running apps float free on the workspace as draggable icons.
  • File Viewer: the NeXT Workspace file browser is back — shelf drawers, a current-location path strip, a grid of your apps and TV streams, and the authentic left-side scroller. It opens on its own when the theme starts.
  • Change any dock icon: right-click a dock or app tile and pick from 120 authentic NeXT “Fleet” icons or your own image, with a “fill the whole tile” option.
  • TV in themed windows: the Classic Themed Window for TV streams now wears the NeXT window chrome too, alongside BeOS, Mac OS 9, Windows XP and System 6.
  • Stable theme identity: renaming or duplicating a theme keeps its wallpaper, dock position and other settings; your existing settings migrate automatically.
  • Fixes: bringing a running app back to the front from its NeXT icon now works reliably, and the System Tweaks and wallpaper restores round-trip correctly.

item.title: Version 2.2
item.description:
RetroMac 2.2: please update manually, one time

This release includes a technical change to how updates are delivered, so your copy can’t install it automatically. Please download 2.2 from the button below and drag it into your Applications folder, just this once. After that, automatic updates work as normal again.

  • Authentic Mac System 6: true 1-bit black & white theme.
  • Warcraft I + II: play them natively with your own game data.
  • Mac OS X boot animation for the Mac OS X and Snow Leopard themes.
  • Clearer Pro unlocks and assorted polish.

item.title: Version 2.0
item.description:
RetroMac 2.0 — themed mouse cursors for every OS

  • Themed mouse cursors: each theme can replace your whole system cursor — the classic Mac pointer with its ticking wristwatch (System 6) or rotating spinner (System 9), the Mac OS X Aqua set with the spinning beach ball, Windows XP, and the retro Windows 3.1 pointers. Toggle it under Settings ▸ Dock ▸ “Match cursor”; your own cursor is captured and restored exactly when the theme goes off.
  • Windows XP cursor sizes: pick Normal, Large or XL while the XP theme is active.
  • BeOS, unified: “BeOS” and “BeOS Classic” are now one theme, with a Dock-style switch between the corner Deskbar and a regular dock.
  • Per-theme icon sizes: the dock and desktop icon-size sliders are remembered per theme.
  • Setup Assistant: opt in (on by default) to matching the macOS colour scheme and the themed cursor.
  • Fixes: the menu-bar Apple logo resets when a theme (or the app) turns off, the System 6 Control Strip is fully opaque with a new boot splash, plus TV-Tube and Duke Nukem / GZDoom launch fixes.

item.title: Version 1.9.7
item.description:
RetroMac 1.9.7 — two new Mac themes, a retro TV & matching system looks

  • New theme — Mac OS 6 classic: a black-and-white System 6 desktop with 1-bit icons, selectable 8×8 desktop patterns, Chicago/Geneva fonts, a Control Strip that can switch to a 2D Platinum dock, and monochrome app icons.
  • Mac OS 9 merged + Platinum widgets: the old “Mac OS 9.2” is now a Platinum-dock option inside Mac OS 9 Classic; every Mac OS 9/6 desktop widget got a pixel-faithful Platinum title bar with working close/collapse/zoom.
  • TV Tube mode: one click turns your streams into a floating retro TV — a free-standing TV in a window, or fullscreen on an external display with a downloadable bezel and the Joel GDV-NTSC shader; right-click to change channel, shader, bezel or TV set.
  • Themes match your Mac: optional per-theme macOS appearance + accent (Graphite for Mac OS …) and a matching Terminal profile (DOS green, BeOS, Classic Mac); your originals are remembered and restored. A crown marks the special themes.
  • Real screensavers: install Pipes, FlowerBox, Flying Toasters and Flurry as genuine macOS .saver modules.
  • More: unified Mac dock icon sizes (desktop icons follow the size slider), Snow Leopard / Mountain Lion shown as “Mac OS …”, sturdier crash recovery, and many smaller fixes.

item.title: Version 1.9.6
item.description:
RetroMac 1.9.6 — a meaner DOOM dock, a 60% smaller download & fixes

  • DOOM theme, real firefights: authentic muzzle-flash animations for every weapon, a Plasma bolt stream, rocket & new BFG explosions, and charging Lost Souls that frag the Slayer if he shoots too late — he now only dies to demons or your mouse, with the full 6-frame fall.
  • 60% smaller download: an asset diet shrank the app from ~151 MB to ~61 MB — same themes, faster downloads and updates.
  • Skippable boot videos: a click or key now skips the Windows XP / 98 / Mac boot sequences straight to the desktop.
  • External displays: the retro menu-bar Apple logo sits correctly on extended monitors.
  • Magnification polish: the running-app dot stays centred under its icon on the Mac OS X / Snow Leopard docks; Snow Leopard joins the special themes.
  • Respects your settings: Retro Mode restores only what it hid (your own Dock auto-hide / hidden desktop icons stay), and the CRT Lite overlay sticks to one window per app.

item.title: Version 1.9.5
item.description:
RetroMac 1.9.5 — a new DOOM theme, a 24-hour clock & lots of fixes

  • New theme — Maiks Favourite II (DOOM): a pixel Doom Slayer patrols the dock (runs, switches weapons, fires, gets fragged) and blasts a Lost Soul that flies in. Hover him to frag him, click the DOOM logo tile to launch DOOM, plus a new “Apple Hell” menu-bar logo.
  • 24-hour clock: new option for the dock and deskbar clocks, plus a digital readout under the analog Clock widget that follows it.
  • Retro menu-bar Apple: Rainbow, Aqua, Aqua Classic or the new Apple Hell logo — cycle it from the flyout, with per-theme defaults.
  • Reliability: your real Dock reliably returns after turning a theme off and never peeks out beside the retro dock; Mac OS X / Snow Leopard magnification no longer reacts outside the dock; the floating launcher stays clickable beside a dock.
  • More: corrected rocket / death sprites, CPU monitor wording fix, and a clearer privacy & offline note in About.

item.title: Version 1.9.2
item.description:
RetroMac 1.9.2 — a retro menu-bar Apple, iPhone camera & a smoother Dock

  • Retro menu-bar Apple: cover the system Apple with the classic Rainbow, Aqua or Aqua Classic logo — cycle it from the flyout. Snow Leopard and Mac OS 9 pick fitting defaults.
  • iPhone as a camera: use your iPhone (Continuity Camera) or any webcam as the CRT-shaded virtual camera — the source list updates live as devices connect.
  • Smoother Dock + Snow Leopard 3D: fluid, real-Dock-style magnification, a corrected Snow Leopard 3D glass shelf, and no more background windows jumping to the front on a theme switch.
  • “Dock only” & calmer themes: Dock only restyles just the dock; the retro TV window and full-screen shader behave reliably, even across Spaces.
  • Dock Mode & quick launcher: show RetroMac in the Dock plus a floating button; one click switches themes and toggles the shader or camera.
  • More: Windows 98/XP taskbar, shaders on every display, GDV-NTSC “Retro Crisis” shaders, softer phosphor masks, paste-able license field, and many fixes.

item.title: Version 1.9.1.1
item.description:
RetroMac 1.9.1.1 — iPhone camera, a true “Dock only” & lots of fixes

  • iPhone as a camera source: pick your iPhone (Continuity Camera) or any webcam in Settings ▸ Camera & Streaming — the list updates live as devices connect, and the CRT shader runs on the feed.
  • “Dock only” really means dock only: switching a theme with Dock only on no longer touches your wallpaper, desktop icons, widgets or boot splash, and won’t start a full-screen shader.
  • Multi-monitor Lite shaders: the lightweight (Lite) presets now appear on the display you select, not just the main one.
  • TV windows behave: the retro TV window no longer borrows the last used theme’s menu bar / chrome when no theme is active.
  • Tidier quick-access flyout: the shader toggle and preset dropdown now stay correct after switching presets; active theme highlighted correctly; Settings/Quit are clean icons; floating launcher on by default.
  • Dock fixes: clicking a Dock tile reliably brings a running app’s window to the front; correct flyout & Dock-Mode icons across themes; desktop-icon visibility now respects other apps.

item.title: Version 1.9.0
item.description:
RetroMac 1.9 — Dock launcher, taskbar tabs & shaders on every screen

  • Dock Mode & quick launcher: optionally show RetroMac in the Dock; click its icon for a slim launcher to switch themes and toggle the shader or virtual camera. Turn it on in Settings ▸ Dock.
  • Authentic Windows taskbar: Windows 98 and XP now show one elongated taskbar button per open window — click to minimize or restore, just like the real thing.
  • Shaders on all your displays: the CRT shader now works on secondary monitors — “All Displays” lights up every screen, not just the main one.
  • New Retro Crisis shaders + fixes: two GDV-NTSC “Retro Crisis” looks (Composite & RGB), and the classic 98.js desktop apps (Notepad, Paint, Minesweeper…) work again.
  • Quick fix: the Settings, Quit and Retro Mode icons in the menu could go missing on a dark desktop — they’re back and reliable.

item.title: Version 1.8.2
item.description:
RetroMac 1.8.2

  • Webcam lower-third fixes: the on-screen name bar no longer flickers, the Late Night (Gold) / Newsroom style now follows your setting, and long names fit the bar.
  • Built-in diagnostics: Settings ▸ About ▸ Diagnostics captures a log you can copy or save — making display, camera and dock issues much easier to track down.
  • Plus stability hardening: the system Dock reliably comes back after quitting, and assorted dock/window fixes.

item.title: Version 1.8.1
item.description:
RetroMac 1.8 — new Special Themes, boot screens & screensavers

  • New Special Themes: Windows 98 (with classic games and sheep.exe!), Windows XP, and Mac OS X with its glossy Aqua look — plus classic apps like Internet Explorer, Notepad and Paint.
  • Boot screens: authentic startup videos when you switch to Windows XP, Windows 98 or Mac OS 9 — click to skip to the desktop.
  • Classic screensavers: a per-theme saver (3D Pipes, FlowerBox, Flying Toasters, Flurry) — pick yours in Settings ▸ Screensaver.
  • Smarter minimize into the themed dock, new CPU Monitor & Desktop Clock widgets, plus widget, dock and stability fixes throughout.

item.title: Version 1.8.0
item.description:
RetroMac 1.8 — three new Special Themes, and even more retro vibes

  • New Special Themes — true to the originals: Windows 98 (with classic games and sheep.exe!), Windows XP, and Mac OS X with its glossy Aqua look.
  • Surf the past: under Windows XP and Windows 98 you can now browse the web with Internet Explorer — just like back in the day.
  • Smarter minimize: windows now minimize into the right dock — the themed dock instead of the system Dock.
  • New widgets & lots of polish: fresh widgets like the CPU Monitor and Desktop Clock, plus stability improvements and a ton of detail work.

item.title: Version 1.7.3
item.description:
RetroMac 1.7.3

  • Clock widget: now remembers its last position and no longer jumps on screen when opened.
  • BeOS Classic: drag the clock by its yellow tab again.
  • CPU widget: opens directly at its saved spot — no more visible jump.
  • Dock right-click now offers “RetroMac Settings” and “Quit RetroMac”.

item.title: Version 1.7.2
item.description:
RetroMac 1.7.2

  • Clock widget: a themed analog clock (BeOS, Mac OS 9, Windows XP, Maiks Favourite) — open it from the deskbar/taskbar clock or a desktop icon.
  • Maiks Favourite: pixel-art macOS window chrome for the CPU widget, App Folder, Music (TV streams) folder and the Downloads dock fan.
  • Menu polish: themes and shaders sorted alphabetically; a crown marks the special themes; the permission-free “Lite” shaders sit right under Free.
  • Stronger LCD Lite shader, clean start (nothing auto-activated), and numerous fixes.

item.title: Version 1.7.0
item.description:
RetroMac 1.7 — The big themes overhaul

  • Themes Overhaul — BeOS, Windows XP & Mac OS 9: a massive rework, as close to the originals as possible — including a native CPU widget and authentically styled windows in each theme.
  • New theme “Maiks Favourite”: an animated Pac-Man dock and live previews of your running apps.
  • Webcam support stabilized: more reliable virtual-camera toggling and retro effects.
  • Stability & fixes: numerous bug fixes and general stability improvements.

item.title: Version 1.3
item.description:
RetroMac 1.3

  • Dock auto-hide: reclaim screen space on 1080p monitors — dock slides in on mouse proximity
  • Freedoom: free Doom experience with native CRT shader (auto-download)
  • Quake 1 & 2 via RetroArch with CRT shader and WASD controls
  • Native PK3 shaders for Duke Nukem 3D and Shadow Warrior (zero input lag)
  • Removed all overlay-based game shaders — native engine shaders only

item.title: Version 1.1
item.description:
RetroMac 1.1

  • Automatic updates via Sparkle
  • Fixed theme switching crash (BeOS to Snow Leopard)
  • Dynamic trash icon (empty/full state)
  • Improved Screen Recording permission onboarding
  • User-friendly error messages for missing permissions
